title: TRIM: Hybrid Inference via Targeted Stepwise Routing in Multi-Step Reasoning Tasks
cost_reduction_reported: On MATH-500 simplest threshold policy gives 5x higher cost efficiency than prior routing methods; advanced policies match the strong model using 80% fewer expensive-model tokens; up to 6x higher cost efficiency on AIME
summary: TRIM routes only the reasoning steps that are likely to derail a solution to a large model, letting a small model write routine continuations. A PRM flags risky steps, and policies range from simple thresholds to long-horizon policies that reason about accuracy-cost trade-offs under step-correctness uncertainty.
key_idea: Escalate only the critical steps (as flagged by a PRM) to the big model.
relevance_rationale: Clean step-level big/small routing with strong cost numbers; math reasoning rather than tool-use agents, but the mechanism maps directly to per-step agent escalation.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"stepwise" AND ti:routing; also cited-by lee-2025-steer

title: MTRouter: Cost-Aware Multi-Turn LLM Routing with History-Model Joint Embeddings
cost_reduction_reported: On ScienceWorld surpasses GPT-5 while reducing total cost by 58.7%; on HLE competitive accuracy with 43.4% lower cost than GPT-5
summary: MTRouter selects which model to call at every turn of a multi-turn, long-horizon task under a fixed budget. It embeds the interaction history jointly with candidate models and learns a turn-level utility estimator from logged trajectories; it makes fewer model switches than prior multi-turn routers and shows emergent model specialization.
key_idea: Per-turn model selection learned offline from logged agent trajectories via history-model joint embeddings.
relevance_rationale: Directly addresses per-turn routing inside agent loops learned from trajectories (sub-themes a and c), with cost-quality numbers vs a frontier model.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"LLM routing" AND abs:"multi-turn"

title: From Myopic Selection to Long-Horizon Awareness: Sequential LLM Routing for Multi-Turn Dialogue
summary: DialRouter treats model selection across a multi-turn dialogue as a sequential decision problem. It runs MCTS over dialogue branches induced by different model choices, then distills a lightweight routing policy from the high-reward search trajectories so that no online search is needed at inference.
key_idea: Long-horizon sequential routing for multi-turn interactions, distilled from MCTS search.
relevance_rationale: Per-turn routing with delayed reward; dialogue rather than tool-using agents, and no headline cost number in the abstract.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"LLM routing" AND abs:"multi-turn"

title: CodeRescue: Budget-Calibrated Recovery Routing for Coding Agents
cost_reduction_reported: In GPT-5.4-nano/GPT-5.4 setting, one CRC-calibrated frontier point exceeds always-escalate solve rate while using 35% of its mean recovery cost (held-out failures from five coding benchmarks)
summary: After a coding agent fails, CodeRescue decides whether to spend more cheap-model recovery attempts or to escalate to the expensive model. A supervised router is trained on execution rollouts, and a conformal risk-control layer picks a deployment cost penalty without retraining, giving marginal expected-cost control.
key_idea: Post-failure recovery routing: cheap retry vs escalate, calibrated to a budget with conformal risk control.
relevance_rationale: Exactly the per-step escalation decision inside coding agents, learned from rollouts, with a concrete cost-quality result.

title: WebRouter: Query-specific Router via Variational Information Bottleneck for Cost-sensitive Web Agent
cost_reduction_reported: 87.8% lower operational cost vs GPT-4o baseline with 3.8% accuracy drop on five WebVoyager websites
summary: WebRouter is a router for LLM-driven web agents whose prompts combine goals, action histories and page state. It is trained with a cost-aware variational information bottleneck that compresses the prompt while penalizing expected cost, and it chooses a model per agent query.
key_idea: Cost-aware information-bottleneck router for web-agent calls.
relevance_rationale: Routing for web agents with a large measured cost reduction.

title: Think Short, Defer Smart, Act, and Repeat: Calibrated Reasoning and Uncertainty-Aware Deferral for Edge LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Per-episode thinking compute reduced 43%-65% vs deferral-only baselines on HotpotQA, MBPP and household-robot tasks, with certified reward and cloud-call-rate guarantees
summary: TSDS targets ReAct agents running on edge devices. A convergence probe stops on-device reasoning once the intended action stabilizes, and a perplexity rule defers uncertain actions to a cloud model; both thresholds are jointly calibrated on episode trajectories with Learn-Then-Test for finite-sample guarantees on reward and cloud-call rate.
key_idea: Per-action deferral from a small local model to a cloud model inside ReAct loops, with statistical guarantees.
relevance_rationale: Per-step small-to-large deferral inside a ReAct loop with certified cost control.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"deferral" AND abs:"LLM agent"

title: AdaptEvolve: Improving Efficiency of Evolutionary AI Agents through Adaptive Model Selection
cost_reduction_reported: Average 37.9% lower total inference cost while retaining 97.5% of upper-bound accuracy of static large-model baselines
summary: AdaptEvolve picks, at each generation step of an evolutionary refinement agent, which model in a pool is capable enough. It uses the model's own generation confidence as a real-time solvability estimate, acting as a confidence-driven cascade.
key_idea: Confidence-driven per-step model selection inside evolutionary agent loops.
relevance_rationale: Step-level model selection in an agent loop with explicit cost-accuracy trade-off.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"model selection" AND ti:agent

title: Don't Solve, Just Compare: Tiny Advisors for Runtime Intervention in LLM Agents
summary: COTA adds a 0.5B comparator to an LLM agent at runtime. The comparator judges the actor's proposed action against alternatives and returns non-binding advice, rather than acting as a costly expert solver or task-capable critic. It is trained from counterfactual branches with the same prefix.
key_idea: A tiny comparator model as a cheap runtime advisor in place of a big expert model.
relevance_rationale: Big-small collaboration inside agent loops, with the small model taking a cheap supervisory role; the abstract claims the best performance-cost trade-off but gives no number.
found_via: arXiv query ti:advisor AND abs:"LLM" AND abs:agent AND abs:cost

title: SPIKE: An Adaptive Dual Controller Framework for Cost-Efficient Long-Horizon Game Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Token consumption reduced 54.9% and latency 40.8%; +5.0 pp SR and +9.3 pp budgeted SR over strongest baselines on StarDojo Lite-100
summary: SPIKE splits a long-horizon game agent into a low-frequency strategic controller and a token-budgeted reactive controller. An event trigger decides when to escalate from reactive execution to strategic reasoning, so the expensive reasoning is reused across stable stretches.
key_idea: Event-triggered escalation from a cheap reactive controller to an expensive strategic controller.
relevance_rationale: Per-step escalation policy with cost numbers; the controllers differ in reasoning mode, not necessarily in model.

title: Think Fast and Slow: Step-Level Cognitive Depth Adaptation for LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: With Qwen2.5-7B, 82.3% success on ALFWorld/ScienceWorld, beating GPT-4o (+40.3%) and o3 (+18.3%) while using 62% fewer tokens
summary: CogRouter trains an agent to choose among four levels of cognitive depth at each step, from instinctive responses to strategic planning. Training combines cognition-aware SFT with an RL stage that does step-level credit assignment via confidence-weighted advantages.
key_idea: Per-step choice of reasoning depth learned with step-level credit assignment.
relevance_rationale: Step-level compute allocation inside agents, which is analogous to step-level model routing; covers sub-themes (a) and (f).
found_via: arXiv query ti:"fast and slow" AND ti:agent

title: DualSpec: Accelerating Deep Research Agents via Dual-Process Action Speculation
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 3.28x end-to-end speedup with accuracy comparable to fully reasoning agents
summary: DualSpec observes that in deep-research agents Search actions are high-entropy and need explicit reasoning, whereas Visit actions are low-entropy and depend mainly on model capacity. It speculates actions heterogeneously by action type and verifies them with a lightweight confidence-based semantic checker.
key_idea: Assign different speculation/reasoning resources by action type in agent loops.
relevance_rationale: Shows action-type heterogeneity in capacity needs, which is direct evidence for step-type routing; the gain reported is latency.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"speculative" AND ti:"actions" AND ti:agent

title: HDLFORGE: A Two-Stage Multi-Agent Framework for Efficient Verilog Code Generation with Adaptive Model Escalation
cost_reduction_reported: 91.2% and 91.8% Pass@1 on VerilogEval Human/V2 with roughly 50% lower median latency
summary: HDLFORGE runs a medium-sized coder by default and escalates to an ultra-large model only when cheap diagnostics (compilation, lint, smoke tests) give a low calibrated score. A formal agent turns bounded-model-checking traces into micro-tests.
key_idea: Diagnostics-gated escalation from medium to ultra-large models in a multi-agent coding pipeline.
relevance_rationale: Agentic escalation using execution signals; domain is Verilog.

title: Local-Splitter: A Measurement Study of Seven Tactics for Reducing Cloud LLM Token Usage on Coding-Agent Workloads
cost_reduction_reported: Local routing + prompt compression gives 45-79% cloud token savings on edit- and explanation-heavy coding-agent workloads; full tactic set incl. draft-review gives 51% on RAG-heavy
summary: A measurement study of seven tactics for cutting cloud-LLM tokens when a small local model triages requests in front of a frontier model in coding agents: local routing, compression, semantic caching, local draft with cloud review, minimal diffs, intent extraction and batching with prompt caching. The tactics are delivered via an MCP/OpenAI-compatible shim.
key_idea: Small local model as a triage layer in front of a frontier model for coding agents; the best tactic mix depends on the workload.
relevance_rationale: Practical big-small split for coding agents, with measured token and dollar savings and open-source tooling.
found_via: Semantic Scholar query "per-turn model routing coding agent"

title: Evaluating Performance Drift from Model Switching in Multi-Turn LLM Systems
summary: The paper measures what happens when a multi-turn system switches models mid-interaction, so that a later model must continue a prefix written by a different model. Even a single-turn handoff moves Multi-IF strict success by -8 to +13 pp; the effect decomposes into per-model prefix influence and suffix susceptibility terms, which explain about 70% of the variance.
key_idea: Mid-conversation model handoffs cause significant, model-pair-specific drift.
relevance_rationale: Key risk evidence for per-step routing; complements ganz-2026-handoff-tax.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"model switching" AND abs:llm

title: Think Big, Search Small: Where Capacity Matters in Hierarchical Search Agents?
cost_reduction_reported: Scaling delegation backbone improves EM ~11 points vs ~2.6 for execution; a 1.7B distilled executor matches a frontier sub-agent with 37% fewer sub-agent tokens
summary: The authors factor hierarchical search agents into delegation, execution and answer-generation roles and sweep model capacity per role. Decomposition is the capacity bottleneck, while execution can be downsized; a 1.7B executor trained by quality-filtered trajectory distillation matches a frontier executor.
key_idea: Put capacity in the planner/delegator and downsize the executor.
relevance_rationale: A controlled planner-big/executor-small study with measured numbers (sub-theme b).
found_via: arXiv query ti:"big-little" OR ti:"big and small" AND abs:agent

title: An Information Theoretic Perspective on Agentic System Design
signals_used: mutual information between context and compression
cost_reduction_reported: A 7B Qwen-2.5 compressor is 1.6x more accurate, 4.6x more concise and conveys 5.5x more MI per token than its smaller sibling (abstract)
summary: The paper models agentic systems in which small compressor LMs summarize raw context for larger predictor LMs as a noisy channel. It proposes a mutual-information estimator that predicts downstream performance independent of task, and finds that larger compressors are both more accurate and more token-efficient; this guides how to size each role.
key_idea: Choose compressor/predictor sizes in multi-LM agents by mutual information rather than task-specific sweeps.
relevance_rationale: A principled analysis of small-worker/large-predictor splits, the core pattern behind Deep Research and Claude Code style systems.

title: Terminus-4B: Can a Smaller Model Replace Frontier LLMs at Agentic Execution Tasks?
cost_reduction_reported: Up to ~30% lower main-agent token usage vs No-Subagent baseline with no performance impact on SWE-Bench Pro and internal SWE-Bench C#
summary: Terminus-4B is a Qwen3-4B model post-trained with SFT and judge-reward RL to act as the terminal-execution subagent of a coding agent, a role usually filled by a frontier model. It isolates verbose build and test output from the main agent's context and closes most of the gap to frontier subagents.
key_idea: Replace frontier subagents for narrow roles (terminal execution) with a fine-tuned 4B SLM.
relevance_rationale: Direct evidence that a specific subagent role can be downscaled to a small model in production-style coding agents.

title: Compute Allocation for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Re-ranking gains +7.5 NDCG@10 from stronger models while query expansion gains only +1.1 from weak to strong (BRIGHT, Gemini 2.5 family)
summary: Studies how to spend compute across the stages of reasoning-intensive retrieval pipelines for agents by varying model size, thinking and re-ranking depth per stage. Strong models matter for re-ranking but not query expansion, and thinking helps little at either stage.
key_idea: Stage-specific model sizing: spend capacity on re-ranking, not query expansion.
relevance_rationale: Controlled per-stage capacity allocation evidence for agent pipelines.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"compute allocation" AND abs:agent

title: The Collaboration Gap
summary: A maze benchmark that isolates collaboration among heterogeneous agents shows that models strong when solo often degrade when paired. A relay in which a stronger agent starts and then hands off to a weaker one closes much of the gap.
key_idea: Strong-first, weak-later relay mitigates the heterogeneous collaboration gap.
relevance_rationale: Evidence on ordering big and small models across the steps of a shared task.

title: INFRAMIND: Infrastructure-Aware Multi-Agent Orchestration
summary: INFRAMIND argues that multi-agent orchestrators and learned routers ignore serving-infrastructure state, so preferred models queue up while equally capable alternatives sit idle. It feeds noisy runtime signals into planning, per-step routing and scheduling decisions for multi-agent pipelines on shared GPU clusters.
key_idea: Make per-step model routing in MAS aware of live serving load.
relevance_rationale: Extends MasRouter-style routing with infrastructure signals relevant to production cost and latency.

title: Hetero-Designer: Automated Design of Multi-Agent Systems with Heterogeneous LLMs
summary: Hetero-Designer introduces automated design of multi-agent systems built from heterogeneous LLMs, jointly choosing roles and which LLM fills each role per query, aiming for cost-effective systems. It encodes dependencies among queries, LLMs and roles to search this joint space efficiently.
key_idea: Automated joint design of topology, roles and per-role LLM choice for heterogeneous MAS.
relevance_rationale: Directly the role-level model-assignment problem; ACL 2026.

title: Mo'Models, Mo'Problems: How to best select model pools when designing Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Evaluates eight strategies for picking candidate models for multi-agent systems, for routing-based and aggregation-based (voting, judge) architectures. Growing the candidate pool often pushes performance below the best single model; selecting within one model family worked best.
key_idea: Bigger heterogeneous model pools often hurt MAS; select candidates carefully.
relevance_rationale: Cautionary evidence for heterogeneous model assignment.

title: SciOrch: Learning to Orchestrate Expert LLMs for Solving Frontier Multimodal Scientific Reasoning Tasks
summary: SciOrch trains an 8B orchestrator to decompose scientific questions, delegate sub-problems to selected commercial frontier models via API, and synthesize the answer. Because each action is an expensive API call, the authors replace online RL rollouts with MCTS-based data collection.
key_idea: Small trained orchestrator delegating sub-problems to frontier APIs.
relevance_rationale: ToolOrchestra-style small-orchestrator/big-worker design; cost is treated mainly as a training constraint.

title: TRINITY: An Evolved LLM Coordinator
summary: Trinity uses a ~0.6B coordinator plus a ~10K-parameter head, optimized with separable CMA-ES, that at each turn assigns a Thinker, Worker or Verifier role to a chosen LLM. It beats individual models and prior methods, reaching 86.2% on LiveCodeBench.
key_idea: Tiny evolved coordinator assigns roles and models per turn.
relevance_rationale: Per-turn role+model assignment by a small coordinator; quality-focused rather than cost-focused.

title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report
summary: Sakana Fugu is a family of orchestrator LMs trained to read a query and devise an agentic scaffold over a team of LLM agents. Training combines fine-tuning, evolutionary search and RL, and the report describes the infrastructure for running it as a production service, with a latency-balanced and a quality-maximizing variant.
key_idea: Productized orchestrator model that builds per-query multi-model scaffolds.
relevance_rationale: An industry technical report on learned multi-model orchestration; a cost-quality variant split but no cost numbers in the abstract.

title: Learning What to Activate: Combinatorial Capability Allocation for Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents
summary: CoCA learns to activate a cost-sensitive subset of specialized capabilities (perception, retrieval, reasoning, verification, execution) at each stage of a long-horizon multimodal agent. A stronger teacher compares marginal capability values on student-visited states; the policy is distilled on-policy and refined with trajectory RL on success and activation cost.
key_idea: Per-stage combinatorial selection of which specialist modules to run, trading success against activation cost.
relevance_rationale: Stage-level allocation of expensive components learned with cost-aware RL.

title: Optimizing Agentic AI Applications Under Budget Constraints
summary: Formulates configuring a multi-step agentic pipeline as choosing one (agent, inference method, parameter) triple per task from a heterogeneous pool of LLMs and SLMs. The objective maximizes end-to-end quality under global time and energy budgets and is solved as a MILP plus complementary methods, accounting for error propagation across steps.
key_idea: MILP-based per-step model/config selection under global budgets.
relevance_rationale: Per-step heterogeneous model assignment under explicit budgets (sub-themes b and e).

title: Rethinking the Value of Multi-Agent Workflow: A Strong Single Agent Baseline
cost_reduction_reported: Single-agent execution matches homogeneous workflows with KV-cache reuse efficiency; OneFlow reduces inference costs vs automatic multi-agent design frameworks
benchmarks: seven benchmarks (coding, math, QA, domain reasoning, planning/tool use)
summary: Shows that homogeneous multi-agent workflows, where all agents share one base LLM, can be simulated by a single agent in multi-turn conversation at equal accuracy while reusing the KV cache. The proposed OneFlow tailors workflows for single-agent execution; the authors note that truly heterogeneous workflows are where multi-agent value may remain.
key_idea: Homogeneous MAS is largely reducible to one agent; heterogeneity is what matters.
relevance_rationale: Key baseline for deciding when multi-agent or multi-model splits are worth it.

title: Retrieval-Conditioned Topology Selection with Provable Budget Conservation for Multi-Agent Code Generation
summary: RGAO extracts a structural-complexity vector from a code index before choosing the orchestration topology for a multi-agent coding system, whose subagents operate under formal six-dimensional budget contracts. The claimed contribution is provable budget conservation under dynamic topology selection.
key_idea: Complexity-conditioned topology routing with formal subagent budgets.
relevance_rationale: Budgeted subagent orchestration; mainly a formal/architectural contribution.

title: CALM: A Self-Adaptive Orchestration Approach for QoS-Aware Routing in Small Language Model based Systems
summary: CALM is a MAPE-K self-adaptive loop that monitors queries and QoS metrics of a fleet of specialized SLMs, then routes each query to the most suitable one and adapts continuously as workloads drift.
key_idea: Self-adaptive orchestration of a fleet of SLMs.
relevance_rationale: SLM-fleet routing from a software-engineering view; query-level.
found_via: arXiv query ti:orchestrator AND abs:"small" AND abs:"cost" AND abs:LLMs

title: Optimizing NetGPT via Routing-Based Synergy and Reinforcement Learning
summary: For edge-deployed network agents, structured tool-calling requests are routed to a cloud or edge agent by a scoring policy that provably reduces to a monotone fallback threshold in bandwidth and RTT. Cloud-routed data is then used for schema-preserving RL to improve the edge agent over time.
key_idea: Edge/cloud routing of tool calls with self-improvement of the small edge agent from cloud traces.
relevance_rationale: Combines routing of tool calls with distillation from routed traffic (sub-themes c and d).

title: History Matters: Meta-policy Delegation with Heterogeneous Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Studies MARL-trained delegation among heterogeneous agents with different capabilities and operating costs, so that tasks are completed under resource constraints. Policies depend on interaction history, and the paper also covers prescribed delegation topologies.
key_idea: MARL delegation among heterogeneous-cost agents.
relevance_rationale: Cost-aware delegation formulation; not LLM-specific benchmarks in abstract.

title: STAR: Failure-Aware Markovian Routing for Multi-Agent Spatiotemporal Reasoning
summary: STAR externalizes routing among heterogeneous specialist agents as a transition matrix conditioned on the current agent, task type and typed failure status. Nominal routes come from experts, and recovery transitions are learned from execution traces.
key_idea: Failure-aware inter-agent routing matrix learned from execution traces.
relevance_rationale: Routing among subagents learned from traces; not cost-focused.

title: AgentBetta: Verification-Driven Adaptive Configuration of an AI Nano-Agent through Selective Expansion and Verified Contraction
cost_reduction_reported: Median context allocation reduced from 64,000 to 8,000 characters and tool exposure from five to zero at 91.38% verified success on AB-ConfigBench
summary: AgentBetta treats an agent's model capability, context, tools, permissions and memory as an executable configuration. It starts minimal, expands selectively when verification diagnoses a deficiency, and contracts counterfactually after success.
key_idea: Verification-driven expand/contract of agent configuration, including model capability.
relevance_rationale: Adaptive per-task resource provisioning for agents.

title: Small Reasoning Models are Instruction Followers in Function Calling
summary: IFFC moves function-calling logic out of the main LLM into a dedicated smaller model that works in a plain instruction-following format. It beats native and prompt-based function calling, especially for reasoning models, and stays robust under aggressive quantization.
key_idea: Delegate tool-call formatting to a small instruction-following model.
relevance_rationale: A function-calling small model inside a larger agent (sub-theme d).

title: CacheRouter: A Dual-Path Tool Routing Architecture with Cache-Preserving Main-Model Isolation for Long-Tail Tool Discovery
cost_reduction_reported: Cache hit rates 90.99% and 95.2%, cutting input cost to ~12.0% and ~8.0% of a no-cache baseline under DeepSeek pricing (55 queries and a 30-turn dialogue)
summary: CacheRouter keeps the main model's tool list small and fixed so its prompt prefix stays cacheable, while a separate router sub-model searches the full tool catalog, runs the chosen tool and returns the result.
key_idea: Offload long-tail tool selection to a router sub-model to keep the main model's cache prefix stable.
relevance_rationale: Subagent offloading as a cost lever that interacts with prompt caching; prototype-scale evaluation.

title: AgentWeave: Routing Before Reasoning for Efficient Function Calling in Tool-Rich Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: 70.18% fewer tools exposed, 61.70% fewer input tokens and 50.95% lower local-model latency vs all-tools exposure on BFCL V4 tasks
summary: AgentWeave is a deterministic pre-inference layer that cuts the candidate tool set before a function-calling model runs, leaving the downstream model unchanged. With a 1.5B model on 48 BFCL tasks it raises success from 0/48 to 6/48.
key_idea: Deterministic tool pre-routing to shrink the action space for small function-calling models.
relevance_rationale: Tool routing as a cost lever; small evaluation.

title: Latency-Quality Routing for Functionally Equivalent Tools in LLM Agents
summary: LQM-ContextRoute is a contextual-bandit router that picks among functionally equivalent tool providers (search APIs, retrievers, LLM backends) under runtime load. It ranks providers by expected quality per service cycle, avoiding the collapse that additive latency-quality rewards cause, and learns online from judge feedback.
key_idea: Online bandit routing among equivalent tool/LLM providers.
relevance_rationale: Tool/backend routing inside agents learned online without gold labels.

title: Outcome-Aware Tool Selection for Semantic Routers: Latency-Constrained Learning Without LLM Inference
summary: OATS improves tool selection in semantic routers at LLM gateways by shifting tool embeddings toward the centroid of queries where each tool historically succeeded, an offline step that adds no serving latency. NDCG@5 on MetaTool rises from 0.869 to 0.940; learned re-rankers help only when outcome data is plentiful.
key_idea: Learn tool routing from historical outcomes offline with zero serving cost.
relevance_rationale: Learning routing from logged outcomes in gateways.

title: Graph-Based Self-Healing Tool Routing for Cost-Efficient LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Matches ReAct correctness while reducing control-plane LLM calls by 93% (9 vs 123) across 19 scenarios
summary: Self-Healing Router treats most agent control flow as deterministic routing over a cost-weighted tool graph with Dijkstra. When a tool fails, edges are reweighted and the path recomputed; the LLM is called only when no feasible path exists.
key_idea: Replace most LLM control decisions with graph routing; call the LLM only to escalate.
relevance_rationale: An architectural cost lever that removes LLM calls from routine steps.

title: Tiny-Critic RAG: Empowering Agentic Fallback with Parameter-Efficient Small Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Routing accuracy comparable to GPT-4o-mini with an order of magnitude lower latency (noise-injected datasets)
summary: Tiny-Critic RAG replaces a large LLM evaluator in agentic RAG with a LoRA-tuned small model that acts as a fast binary gatekeeper over retrieval quality, triggering fallback only when needed.
key_idea: Small LoRA critic as the routing gate in agentic RAG.
relevance_rationale: Small-model gate for a step in an agentic pipeline.
found_via: arXiv query ti:"agentic" AND ti:"efficient" AND ti:"small language models"

title: Inference-Time Budget Control for LLM Search Agents
summary: For search agents under hard caps on both tool calls and tokens, a controller scores each feasible action (retrieve, decompose, commit) by estimated marginal task value per unit budget. A selective finalizer rewrites the answer only for low-risk form errors; budget-dependent penalties drive most of the gain.
key_idea: Value-of-information budget allocation across agent actions under dual hard budgets.
relevance_rationale: Per-task budgeted agent execution (sub-theme e).
found_via: arXiv query ti:"budget" AND ti:agent AND ti:llm

title: Quantifying the Accuracy and Cost Impact of Design Decisions in Budget-Constrained Agentic LLM Search
summary: BCAS is a harness that exposes remaining budget to agentic RAG systems and gates tool use. It measures how search depth, retrieval strategy and completion budget affect accuracy and cost across six LLMs; accuracy saturates after a few searches and hybrid retrieval with light re-ranking helps most.
key_idea: Measurement harness for budget-constrained agentic search design.
relevance_rationale: Budgeted agent-execution evidence.

title: Budgeted Act-or-Defer Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation with Local Reliability Bounds
cost_reduction_reported: Uses 9-12% of the pre-declared wrong-action budget, reaching up to 84% automation and 96% acted-on accuracy on six benchmarks
summary: Frames multi-agent debate deployment as deciding, round by round, whether to act or defer to human review under a user-declared wrong-action budget. A kNN lower confidence bound on correctness, computed from calibration data, sets the act threshold with stated assumptions and diagnostics.
key_idea: Per-round act-or-defer with a declared risk budget for multi-agent deliberation.
relevance_rationale: Budgeted per-round stopping in MAS; deferral is to humans, not to models.

title: More with Less: An Empirical Study of Turn-Control Strategies for Efficient Coding Agents
summary: An empirical study on SWE-bench of turn-control strategies for coding agents: unrestricted, fixed-turn limits with reminders, and dynamic limits. It frames total turn count as a primary lever on cost, since tokens grow with every turn.
key_idea: Turn budgets as a cost lever for coding agents.
relevance_rationale: Budget-constrained agent execution in coding agents; ICSE 2026.
found_via: Semantic Scholar query "per-turn model routing coding agent"

title: Marginal-Contribution Policy Gradients under Filtered Feedback for Multi-Agent LLMs
summary: Proves that shared-reward training of multi-agent LLM systems cannot distinguish agents that matter from ones that do not, and derives gradient-correct marginal-contribution signals identifiable from filtered feedback, with an optimal budget for exact counterfactual evaluations. In GRPO it improves routed GSM8K over winner-take-all training at no extra generation cost.
key_idea: Marginal-contribution credit assignment for routed multi-agent LLMs.
relevance_rationale: Credit assignment theory applicable to deciding which agents matter (sub-theme f).

title: CANTANTE: Optimizing Agentic Systems via Contrastive Credit Attribution
summary: CANTANTE treats configuring multi-agent systems as credit assignment, decomposing system-level rewards into per-agent signals by contrasting rollouts of multiple joint configurations on the same query. Instantiated for prompt optimization, it gets the best average rank vs GEPA and MIPROv2.
key_idea: Contrastive per-agent credit attribution for optimizing agentic configs.
relevance_rationale: Credit attribution that could extend to per-agent model choice.

title: HiveMind: Contribution-Guided Online Prompt Optimization of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
summary: HiveMind quantifies each agent's contribution in an LLM multi-agent system with an efficient DAG-Shapley approximation, then refines prompts of underperforming agents online.
key_idea: Shapley-based per-agent contribution scoring for MAS optimization.
relevance_rationale: Per-agent credit signals usable for deciding where cheaper models are safe.

title: MASPrism: Lightweight Failure Attribution for Multi-Agent Systems Using Prefill-Stage Signals
summary: MASPrism attributes failures in multi-agent executions to source steps using only two prefill passes of a 0.6B model, reading token NLL and attention instead of decoding, and achieves the best results on three of four Who&When/TRAIL subsets.
key_idea: Cheap SLM prefill signals for step-level failure attribution.
relevance_rationale: Low-cost step attribution; a building block for step-level routing decisions.

title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
summary: A systematic evaluation of five multi-agent debate methods on nine benchmarks finds they often fail to beat CoT and self-consistency despite using more compute. Mixing heterogeneous models consistently improves MAD.
key_idea: MAD rarely pays off; model heterogeneity is the reliable improvement.
relevance_rationale: Key evidence on cost-effectiveness of debate and heterogeneous agents (sub-theme g).

title: Heterogeneous LLM Debate Under Adversarial Peers: Honest Gains, Replacement Costs, and Resilience
summary: Measures how a heterogeneous peer changes honest agents' revisions in debate. An honest cross-family peer cuts harmful revision on MATH-hard from 89% to 35% for Llama-3.1-70B defenders, while an adversarial one returns it to 90%.
key_idea: Heterogeneous debate peers help when honest but amplify harm when adversarial.
relevance_rationale: Heterogeneous debate dynamics; no cost numbers.

title: Do Mixed-Vendor Multi-Agent LLMs Improve Clinical Diagnosis?
summary: Compares single-LLM, single-vendor and mixed-vendor multi-agent conversations for clinical diagnosis. Mixed-vendor teams consistently win because they pool complementary inductive biases.
key_idea: Vendor diversity beats homogeneous teams in diagnostic MAS.
relevance_rationale: Heterogeneous-model MAS evidence (quality only).

title: MOSAIC: Efficient Mixture-of-Agent Scheduling via Adaptive Aggregation and Inference Concurrency
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 2.5x expert-stage, 4.23x aggregator-stage and 1.7-2.3x end-to-end speedups vs baseline scheduler, accuracy within 0.1pp (4-GPU system)
summary: MOSAIC schedules Mixture-of-Agents workloads with an ILP that places experts and assigns prompts per worker using offline-profiled costs. It skips the heavy aggregator LLM when experts already agree.
key_idea: Agreement-gated aggregator skipping plus ILP scheduling for MoA.
relevance_rationale: MoA cost study with a selective-skip mechanism (sub-theme g).

title: Differentiable Mixture-of-Agents Incentivizes Swarm Intelligence of Large Language Models
summary: DMoA dynamically activates a sparse subset of agents at each reasoning step through a differentiable, context-aware router, implicitly simulating many communication topologies. Predictive entropy serves as a self-supervised signal for test-time adaptation.
key_idea: Step-wise sparse agent activation via a differentiable router.
relevance_rationale: Step-level agent routing in MoA; efficiency claims are qualitative in the abstract.

title: The Fleet Is the Model: Engineering Collective Intelligence with Fusion-MoA Pioneer R1
summary: Fusion-MoA exposes a governed fleet of heterogeneous model "Cells" as one OpenAI-compatible model, with read-only Analysts and a single Executor holding tool authority. Members can be promoted or rolled back without changing the API. The collective solves 8/10 HMMT problems vs 6/10 for the best single Cell.
key_idea: Operate a heterogeneous model fleet as one governed, evolvable service.
relevance_rationale: Operational architecture for heterogeneous MoA; no cost numbers.

title: Guided Collaboration in Heterogeneous LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Entropy-Based Understanding Assessment and Experience Retrieval
summary: In heterogeneous MAS, strong-weak pairings can underperform weak-weak pairings because of cognitive mismatch. The authors propose entropy-based assessment of the weak agent's understanding to adapt guidance, plus experience retrieval.
key_idea: Strong-weak agent pairs need adaptive guidance to beat homogeneous teams.
relevance_rationale: Evidence on pitfalls of mixing big and small models across roles.

title: The Six Sigma Agent: Achieving Enterprise-Grade Reliability in LLM Systems Through Consensus-Driven Decomposed Execution
cost_reduction_reported: 14,700x reliability improvement over single-agent execution while reducing costs by 80% (three enterprise use cases)
summary: Six Sigma Agent decomposes tasks into atomic actions, runs each n times across diverse cheaper LLMs, and takes a consensus vote with dynamic scaling. Theory shows error falls exponentially in n.
key_idea: Redundant cheap-model micro-agents with voting instead of one expensive model.
relevance_rationale: Cheap-model redundancy as a cost lever; enterprise claims are from an evaluation, not live traffic.

title: The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI
cost_reduction_reported: Harness cuts blended cost per task 41% ($0.21->$0.12), wall-clock 44%, tokens 38% at quality parity (0.78->0.81) across six models on 22 tasks; quality per dollar +82%
summary: A controlled swap that keeps six models fixed and changes only the orchestration layer, comparing a conventional production loop with Writer's agent harness. On this workload the harness moved cost per task more than the whole spread of model choices, and quality gains scaled with model strength.
key_idea: Orchestration harness design is a larger cost lever than model choice.
relevance_rationale: Enterprise evidence that bounds the value of model routing relative to harness design.

title: Progressive Crystallization: Turning Agent Exploration into Deterministic, Lower-Cost Workflows in Production
cost_reduction_reported: Deterministic execution rose 0% to 45% over eight months; per-incident agent cost reduced >70% despite doubling incident volume (production cloud-networking AIOps)
summary: Progressive crystallization promotes repeatedly validated agent behaviors in a production IT-ops system into deterministic workflows, and demotes them on regression. Over eight months on tens of thousands of incidents per month it shifted executions off the LLM.
key_idea: Graduate agent trajectories into deterministic workflows to remove LLM calls.
relevance_rationale: Real production evidence for learning from traces to cut agent cost.

title: ADEPT: adaptive delegation of expert prompts to trained SLMs for agentic AI use cases

relevance_rationale: Production-style evidence for learning delegation from traffic.

title: Measuring Tradeoffs in Multi-Agent Models: a Case Study in Shipping Cost Calculation

key_idea: Reference architecture for heterogeneous model assignment in production agents.

title: fastWorkflow: Closing the Performance Gap Between Small and Frontier Language Models for Conversational Agents
summary: Builds a taxonomy of SLM failure modes in conversational tool-use agents (NLU, tool management, decomposition, reasoning, context) measured on tau-bench, then proposes a dual-mode architecture with a cascaded NLU pipeline to close the gap to frontier models.

cost_reduction_reported: Distilled Flan-T5-small (80M) orchestrator achieves Routing Accuracy Score 0.942 on Indian legal queries
summary: PEARL replaces a GPT-4 orchestrator in a multi-agent RAG system with an 80M Flan-T5 trained on 12,000 GPT-4 routing traces, classifying queries into one of four agent pipeline configurations.

title: What Stops a Small Language Model From Driving a Database Agent
summary: Over eleven days the authors drove a real open-source SQL client's agent mode with 39 local open-weight models (8,199 runs). Most small-model losses came from runs that did call tools, mostly transport/argument-shape failures, and five server-side fixes moved model results substantially without changing any model.
key_idea: Small-model agent failures are often interface failures, not capability gaps.
relevance_rationale: Practical evidence on making SLMs viable inside agents.

title: Agent Skill Framework: Perspectives on the Potential of Small to Medium Language Models in Industrial Environments
summary: Studies whether agent Skills work with small and medium open models in resource-constrained industrial settings. Very small models struggle with skill selection, models around 30B-80B benefit, and thinking variants add GPU cost without much gain.
key_idea: Skills need ~30B+ models; very small models fail at skill selection.
relevance_rationale: Sizing guidance for open models in industrial agents.

title: An Empirical Cost Attribution of Context-Compression Gateways in Multi-Turn Coding Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Tool-schema filtering removes ~21K-57K tokens per turn; content compression saves only ~2% of cache-priced prefix per turn (real Claude Code/Codex sessions)
summary: Instruments a production compression gateway between coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) and frontier LLMs and decomposes the token bill into tool-schema filtering, content compression and history summarization under controlled A/B runs. Only schema filtering is reliably positive once prompt caching is priced in.
key_idea: With prompt caching, compression savings are much smaller than benchmarks imply.
relevance_rationale: Production cost attribution for coding agents; supporting lever.
